response.sql: WITH b AS (SELECT o.timespan, COUNT(*) AS cnt FROM riskandmargin r JOIN orders o ON r.ordervault = o.recordvault GROUP BY o.timespan), s AS (SELECT timespan, cnt, cnt * 1.0 / SUM(cnt) OVER () AS share FROM b), t AS (SELECT timespan, cnt, share, AVG(share) OVER () AS avg_share FROM s) SELECT SUM(cnt) AS total_count, AVG(share) AS avg_share, AVG(share - avg_share) AS avg_excess_over_avg_share FROM t WHERE share > avg_share

assumptions.assumption: orders.recordvault is unique per order, so each risk/margin record matches at most one order and the inner join does not inflate counts.
The NULL time-in-force bucket is a single group, which GROUP BY does by default. The plain average of bucket shares is taken over all buckets, including the NULL one, before filtering.
